projects.name: Mezgeb
projects.tagline: Offline mobile-money ledger for Ethiopian shops
projects.statusNote: Under active development. Builds and tests pass in CI; not yet published on the Play Store.
projects.problem: Small shops in Ethiopia take payment through mobile money and bank apps, and the confirmations arrive as notifications nobody reconciles against who owes the shop.
projects.approach: A notification listener captures payment notifications, because Google Play does not grant READ_SMS to finance apps. A JSON-defined rule engine parses them into a ledger. When no rule matches, the message goes to a review queue, and the shopkeeper teaches a new rule by highlighting the amount.
results: 375 unit tests on the Play flavor, 382 on the sideload flavor, 83 on the parser module.
No INTERNET permission in either flavor, checked against the merged release manifest.
Release APK is 3.07 MB.
learned: The parser scores 100.00% on its holdout (23/23), and the README says plainly that this is worth less than it looks: all samples come from 3 senders and 13 message templates from one person's account.
RECEIVE_SMS was carried for several sessions and then removed, because nothing used it. A restricted permission has to be justified, not kept just in case.
Coverage is 36.1% instruction / 46.1% line, reported rather than gated.

projects.name: Suq
projects.tagline: Offline-first point of sale and inventory
projects.statusNote: Under active development. CI passes on every merge; no public deployment is linked from the repo.
projects.problem: A shop till has to keep selling when the internet and the power go out, and two offline tablets must not overwrite each other's sales when they reconnect.
projects.approach: IndexedDB is the source of truth and Supabase is a replica. Stock is never synced as a quantity: each device appends stock movements, and stock on hand is their sum, so concurrent offline sales commute. Sales are append-only; a mistake becomes a void row, not a deletion.
results: A sale writes to IndexedDB in one transaction and never touches the network.
A sync test suite covers the five failure modes that only appear across multiple devices, including two tablets selling the last unit while offline.
Amharic-first UI, ETB pricing and 80mm thermal receipts.
learned: Last-write-wins silently destroys a sale when two devices sync absolute quantities. Append-only rows avoid the conflict instead of resolving it.
Free hosting tiers have limits that matter for a live shop: Supabase free projects pause after 7 days of inactivity.

facts.quote: Completing a sale never touches the network. It writes to IndexedDB in one transaction

projects.name: DocSearch → Not Alone
projects.tagline: Cited answers from documents, now pivoting to a scripture app
projects.statusNote: Pivoting. The cited-retrieval engine is being repurposed into Not Alone, a scripture app; the original DocSearch evaluation work is complete.
projects.problem: Question answering over documents is only useful if every claim can be traced to a source, and if the system refuses when the documents do not cover the question.
projects.approach: Hybrid retrieval: vector search and Postgres full-text search fused with Reciprocal Rank Fusion. Every claim in the streamed answer carries an inline citation to its source chunk. An evaluation harness measures retrieval and answer quality against a human-reviewed golden set. The pivot, Not Alone, answers a described struggle with the cited story of a holy person who fell the same way and was restored.
results: 91 human-reviewed evaluation questions.
One of four LLM judges validated against human labels: Cohen's kappa 0.80 on a random sample.
Answer correctness 52.4% on the dev split; 24 of 63 answerable questions get a refusal.
learned: Three of four retrieval experiments did nothing, and the config was left unchanged rather than shipping an unmeasured win.
The measurement was wrong three times: a truncated labelling UI, a contaminated unanswerable bucket, and a rubric with no answer for refusals. Each first looked like a system failure.

projects.name: ethiopic-text
projects.tagline: Search and normalization for Ethiopic script
projects.statusNote: Published on npm. Released as 0.x on purpose while linguistic choices wait for a native reader's review.
projects.problem: Ethiopic has homophone consonants that writers use interchangeably, so the same word is spelled two ways and string search silently misses one of them.
projects.approach: Fold the homophone families with codepoint arithmetic rather than a lookup table, in independently importable modules for folding, search, fuzzy matching, transliteration, Geez numerals, phone numbers and money.
results: Zero runtime dependencies; the core is 0.49 KB gzipped.
100% coverage.
learned: Over-collapsing is a worse failure than under-collapsing, so negative tests assert that genuinely different words stay distinct.

facts.quote: TypeScript, zero runtime dependencies, 0.49 KB gzipped for the core.
Zero runtime dependencies, dual ESM/CJS, 100% coverage.
Published as 0.x deliberately
